What We Do

Full-Service Audiology Revenue Cycle Management

Audiology billing requires precise CPT code selection per test type and technology, hearing aid HCPCS coding with correct device classification, cochlear implant procedure billing, and payer-specific benefit verification for hearing device coverage. PMEX manages every element inside your existing audiology workflow.

Audiometric Testing Billing

Pure tone (92551 to 92557), speech (92555 to 92556), and tympanometry (92567) coded per test.

Hearing Aid HCPCS Coding

V5000 to V5299 hearing aid codes billed by device type, ear, and technology level.

Cochlear Implant Billing

Cochlear implant surgery (69930) and programming codes billed with device and mapping CPTs.

Vestibular Evaluation Coding

VNG/ENG testing (92541 to 92548) and VEMP testing coded from the evaluation report.

Hearing Aid Benefit Verification

Payer hearing aid benefit confirmed before fitting, including lifetime limits and device restrictions.

ABR and OAE Testing

Auditory brainstem response (92585) and otoacoustic emissions (92587 to 92588) billed correctly.

Sound Familiar?

Common Audiology Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Comprehensive audiological evaluation billed at basic pure tone level, under-coding the test battery.

PMEX codes the full audiometric battery from the test report, applying the correct CPT for each test performed.

Hearing aid billed with wrong V-code for the device technology level or fitting type.

PMEX confirms the device type and technology level before selecting the correct V5000-series HCPCS code.

Hearing aid benefit not verified before fitting, patient later disputes cost-sharing responsibility.

PMEX verifies the hearing aid benefit, lifetime limit, and covered device types before any fitting appointment.

ABR testing billed at the wrong code for diagnostic vs. screening application.

PMEX distinguishes diagnostic ABR (92585) from screening ABR (92584) and applies the correct code per the test purpose.

Cochlear implant programming visits not billed separately from the device management E/M.

PMEX bills cochlear implant programming (92601 to 92604) separately from the audiology evaluation on programming visits.

Vestibular testing components not individually billed, losing revenue on multi-test VNG sessions.

PMEX bills each VNG component separately from the vestibular test report on every multi-component evaluation.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Audiology Billing

Audiology practices lose 16 to 28 percent of revenue to hearing aid benefit errors, audiometric test under-coding, and device HCPCS mismatches.

PATTERN 01

Hearing Aid Denied, Lifetime Limit Reached

Patient fitted with new hearing aids. Claim submitted. Commercial payer denies: patient exhausted their hearing aid lifetime benefit ($1,500 per ear every 3 years) 18 months ago. Patient was not informed before fitting. Practice absorbs the cost.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX verifies hearing aid benefit remaining, lifetime limit status, and covered device categories before every fitting appointment. Patients are informed of their remaining benefit and out-of-pocket responsibility before the device is ordered.

PATTERN 02

Comprehensive Audiological Evaluation Under-Coded

Patient receives pure tone audiometry, speech discrimination, tympanometry, and acoustic reflex testing. Only 92551 (pure tone screening, $35) submitted instead of 92557 (comprehensive audiological evaluation, $110). $75 per evaluation under-coded.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX codes the audiometric battery from the test report, applying 92557 (comprehensive) when the evaluation includes pure tone, speech, and immittance testing, and individually coding additional tests performed beyond the comprehensive battery.

PATTERN 03

Hearing Aid V-Code Mismatch

Behind-the-ear hearing aid dispensed. V5090 (hearing aid, not otherwise specified) submitted. Payer requires the specific V-code for the device technology level. Correct code: V5261 (programmable BTE). Claim adjusted to lower reimbursement rate.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX applies the correct hearing aid V-code for the specific device dispensed, confirmed against the dispensing record and the payer benefit structure for hearing aid device categories.

Questions

Audiology Billing Questions Answered

92557 covers a comprehensive audiological evaluation including pure tone air and bone conduction, speech recognition, and immittance testing. Additional tests such as OAE (92587 to 92588) and ABR (92585) are billed separately when performed.

Hearing aids are billed using HCPCS V-codes (V5000 to V5299) based on the device type, technology level, and ear. We confirm the correct V-code for the specific device dispensed before submission.

Most commercial plans that cover hearing aids have lifetime limits (typically $1,000 to $3,000 per ear every 3 to 5 years). We verify remaining benefit before every fitting.

Cochlear implant programming uses CPT codes 92601 to 92604 based on whether the patient is a child or adult and whether it is the initial or subsequent programming session. These are billed separately from the audiological evaluation.

Yes. VNG/ENG testing (92541 to 92548) is separately billable from the audiological evaluation when performed at the same visit, as long as each test is separately documented.
